env: A 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell host with Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC credentials, and the VSS repository at `{{repo_root}}`. This eval builds and deploys the alert-verification capability as a delta overlay on the current `alerts` developer profile in `2d_cv` mode. The build label is `at-1`; it is only a directory name and never a Compose profile. Existing profile files under `deploy/docker/` remain authoritative and unmodified. VIOS is reached through the repository-local `vss` CLI per `AGENTS.md` (`uv run --project {{repo_root}}/services/agent --no-dev --extra cli vss`) — `vss configure --base-url http://localhost:${HAPROXY_HOST_PORT:-7777}` once against the ingress origin, then `vss vios list` — never a globally installed `vss` and never a raw VIOS REST probe where a `vss vios` verb exists. This does not change the alert path itself: `alert-bridge` retrieves its own clips internally.

expects.query: Use `/vss-build-vision-ai` to build and deploy this capability from `{{repo_root}}`: "Given a stream, retrieve the relevant clip and verify candidate alerts posted to Kafka. Grounding DINO detections and behavior analytics should be VLM-verified to reduce false positives. Store and publish verified incidents, and make them queryable through the VSS agent with report generation." Use `_builds/at-1/` as the filesystem label, target `{{platform}}`, select the current alerts `2d_cv` profile as the single Foundation, validate the delta, deploy it, and leave it running for verifier probes.
checks: `{{repo_root}}/_builds/at-1/override.env` exists and declares `FOUNDATION=alerts` and the full effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES`. The effective `MODE` is `2d_cv`, which the `alerts` Foundation already sets (`dev-profile-alerts/overrides.env`) — inheriting it satisfies this check, and re-declaring it in the delta would copy an unchanged default, which the skill's smallest-delta contract forbids (AT-1 has no delta-defaults check of its own; IN-2 and IN-3 spell the rule out). What fails is a delta that selects a different mode, or one whose effective `MODE` is not `2d_cv`.

Ignoring order, `COMPOSE_PROFILES` equals exactly the current alerts `2d_cv` set (which already includes `rtvi-vlm` for clip verification): `vss-behavior-analytics-alerts,nvstreamer-alerts,perception-alerts,kibana-init-container-alerts,vss-video-analytics-api-alerts,vss-va-mcp,vss-agent,alert-bridge,phoenix,elasticsearch,elasticsearch-init-container,kafka,kafka-topic-init-container,redis,kibana,logstash,broker-health-check,vss-haproxy-ingress,rtvi-vlm,vss-ui,centralizedb,vst-ingress,sensor-ms,streamprocessing-ms,llm_${LLM_MODE}_${LLM_NAME_SLUG}`.
`COMPOSE_PROFILES` does not contain `at-1`, an aggregate profile, or any invented profile key; every token exists in the current resolved Compose graph.

`_builds/at-1/compose.yml` includes `../../deploy/docker/compose.yml`, and `_builds/at-1/patches/` is absent because the request changes no service definition and every selected service already exists upstream.

`{{repo_root}}/_builds/at-1/` contains the three required primary artifacts (`override.env`, `compose.yml`, and `resolved.yml`) and no copied Foundation `.env`, copied root Compose project, patched source tree, manifest, allow-list, or generated skill bundle.

Resolution uses `containers.env`, the alerts Foundation `.env`, the alerts Foundation `overrides.env`, and `_builds/at-1/override.env` in that order with the build `compose.yml`; it produces a normalized `_builds/at-1/resolved.yml` whose direct `config --quiet`, `config --services`, and `config --images` checks succeed, whose values contain no `/path/to/deploy/docker` or `<HOST_IP>` sentinel, and whose checked-in bind sources exist with the expected file/directory type.

No file under `{{repo_root}}/deploy/docker/` is created, modified or deleted by the agent: no hand edits, and no patch pointing at that tree. The SDRC containers the shipped graph starts write through their own declared mounts — `services/infra/sdrc/log`, `services/infra/sdrc/.wdm-env`, and the `config.yml` / `docker_cluster_config-*.json` rendered under `${SDR_CONTROLLER_CONFIG_PATH}` — and those writes are deployment doing its job, as is `$VSS_APPS_DIR/engines/`, which `dev-profile-alerts/compose.yml` mounts. Anything else appearing under that tree still fails, a data directory above all: `VSS_DATA_DIR` must point outside the repository, so `deploy/docker/data-dir/` is a wrongly chosen path, not an exempt artifact.
The deployment is launched directly from `_builds/at-1/resolved.yml` without Foundation env files, profile flags, or a copied Compose project.
All long-running selected containers are running or healthy, and all selected one-shot initialization containers exit 0.

RT-CV and Behavior Analytics publish candidate alerts, `alert-bridge` can retrieve the corresponding VIOS clip, and the verifier records a `verdict` field on the verified record in Elasticsearch and Kafka. A missing document, or a document with no `verdict` field at all, fails; an empty `info.verdict` passes, which `SKILL.md` calls a valid state on a freestyle deploy. Accept any value the `vss-manage-alerts` references document, because they do not agree with each other: `SKILL.md` lists `confirmed` / `rejected` / `not-confirmed` / `verification-failed` / empty, while `references/integrate-alerts.md` documents `confirmed` / `rejected` / `unverified` for the cv-verification path this build runs — and `references/deploy-alerts.md` treats `unverified` as a real, diagnosable outcome. What fails this check is no verdict recorded at all, not a verdict from whichever of those lists the deployment happens to follow.

The VSS Agent, video-analytics MCP, alert API, and Elasticsearch health endpoints respond successfully, and VIOS answers through the repository-local `vss` CLI (`vss configure --base-url http://localhost:${HAPROXY_HOST_PORT:-7777}` then `vss vios list`) rather than a raw VIOS REST probe — the CLI comes from `uv run --project {{repo_root}}/services/agent --no-dev --extra cli vss`, never a globally installed `vss`.
The final response identifies `alerts` as the Foundation, reports the effective service delta and changed environment knobs, and includes evidence for the alert-verification round trip.
